md_name: CRISPR Perturbation Proteomics Causal Interaction Dataset
md_description: This DAG represents a high-throughput screening workflow in human cancer cell lines where CRISPR-Cas9 knockouts perturb regulatory proteins and mass spectrometry measures downstream changes in protein interactions and signaling. The resulting computational analysis integrates proteomic identifications, knockout validation, and literature support to produce a structured metadata table capturing interacting proteins, causal relationship type, experimental conditions, and supporting references.

human_cancer_cell_line.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic properties of the human cancer cell line itself: identity/origin, biological context, and baseline characteristics relevant before any CRISPR perturbation or proteomic measurement. I excluded culture protocol parameters, assay settings, editing details, lysis/extraction, MS capture settings, raw file properties, and computed analysis fields because those belong to downstream Process, Capture, Signal, or Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were provided here, so I avoided only territory overlap with downstream nodes by keeping the schema focused on what the cell line IS rather than what was done to it.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the cultured human cancer cell line used as the starting biological entity in the workflow, e.g. 'HCT116', 'A549', or an internal sample code. String identifier recorded once for the entity and reused across downstream steps.
Common or repository name of the human cancer cell line, such as a standard ATCC/DSMZ name. Record at the entity level before CRISPR perturbation.
Organism of origin for the cell line. For this DAG the expected value is human, recorded as the biological source of the cultured cells.
Primary tissue or anatomical site from which the cancer cell line was derived, e.g. breast, lung, colon, or prostate. Record as the intrinsic origin of the line, not as a culture condition.
Cancer classification associated with the cell line, such as carcinoma, leukemia, melanoma, or glioblastoma. Record the disease context of the entity before any experimental manipulation.

Known baseline genomic or molecular background of the cell line relevant to interpretation of perturbation results, such as key driver mutations or oncogenic alterations present prior to CRISPR editing.
Repository, vendor, or laboratory source of the cell line, e.g. ATCC, DSMZ, JCRB, or an internal biobank. Record where the unedited entity was obtained.
Repository catalog number or accession identifier for the cell line, formatted as the provider's identifier string, e.g. 'ATCC HTB-96'. Use only for the original entity identity.

Method used to authenticate the identity of the cell line prior to perturbation, e.g. STR profiling, SNP genotyping, or vendor certificate. This describes the entity's verified identity status, not a process parameter.
Brief description of any intrinsic adaptation status of the cell line before the assay, such as adherent vs suspension growth or established laboratory adaptation history.

crisp_cas9_knockout_editing.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included fields describing how the CRISPR-Cas9 knockout editing was performed: editing reagent/system, target selection, delivery/editing parameters, selection/validation-related process outputs, and operator-controlled conditions. I excluded intrinsic cell-line properties because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded edited-cell or validation readout properties because those belong to downstream Entity/Capture/Signal nodes. No already_generated fields were provided, so I kept the schema narrowly within process territory and avoided any output-file or measurement artifact descriptions.

md_schema.descr: CRISPR-Cas9 editing system used for the knockout step, including nuclease variant and any notable construct variant, recorded as the process reagent/system identity (e.g. SpCas9, HiFi Cas9, base editor is not applicable here).

Target gene or regulatory protein gene intentionally disrupted by the CRISPR knockout step, recorded as the designed perturbation target (e.g. EGFR, TP53, MYC). If multiple targets were edited in one batch, record the primary target or use a delimited list.
Guide RNA spacer sequence used for targeting, typically 20 nt plus PAM context if applicable in the record. Record the exact designed sequence associated with the knockout process.

Method used to introduce the CRISPR reagents into the cancer cells, such as lentiviral transduction, electroporation, lipid transfection, or nucleofection. This is a process-setting field controlled during editing.

Concentration of CRISPR editing reagent applied during the knockout process, reported in ng/µL at the point of delivery or mixture preparation. Typical values depend on platform and should reflect the actual editing setup used.

Cell density of the cancer culture at the time of CRISPR editing, reported in cells/mL when reagents were applied. This is an operator-controlled process condition that can affect knockout efficiency.
Duration in hours between reagent delivery and the end of the editing incubation window prior to recovery or selection. Record the actual incubation length used for the knockout step.
Selection reagent, if any, used after CRISPR delivery to enrich edited cells, such as puromycin, blasticidin, or hygromycin. Use 'none' if no selection was applied.
Number of days the selection pressure was maintained after CRISPR delivery to enrich knockout cells, measured in days and recorded at the process stage.

Observed editing efficiency for the knockout process, expressed as the percent of cells or alleles successfully edited in the editing batch before downstream validation. This is a process output quality indicator, not a signal-level readout.

Overall quality assessment of the knockout editing step based on expected perturbation performance, such as whether the edit was acceptable for downstream screening. Use a categorical summary for process-level QC.

edited_cell_population.reasoning: This is an Entity node representing the post-edit biological material, so I included intrinsic properties of the edited cell population: which knockouts are present, whether editing was confirmed at a population level, how heterogeneous the population is, and basic viability/status before downstream assays. I excluded the editing protocol itself because that belongs to the upstream Process node, and I excluded validation readouts, lysis/extraction, and measurement artifacts because those belong to downstream Capture/Signal nodes. I also avoided repeating root-level sample identifiers in line with previously generated fields for the upstream entity and process nodes, and kept the schema focused on what the edited population IS rather than what was done to it.

md_schema.descr: Gene intentionally disrupted in this edited cell population, as carried forward from the CRISPR perturbation step. Record the targeted regulatory protein gene(s) present in the living population before downstream assays.

Zygosity of the edited locus in the cell population, indicating whether the targeted gene is biallelic, monoallelic, or mixed across the population. Record the population-level state after editing and before assay capture.
Whether the edited population is a clonal isolate or a pooled heterogeneous population. Record this as an intrinsic property of the post-edit entity prior to downstream assays.

Whether targeted knockout was confirmed at the entity level before downstream assays, for example by genotyping or screening confirmation. This records the biological status of the edited population, not the validation signal itself.

Estimated viable cell fraction in the edited population immediately before downstream assays, reported as percent viable cells. Typical values are 0-100 and should reflect the state of the entity at the time it is transferred onward.
Passage number of the edited cell population at the time it is used for downstream assays. Record as an integer reflecting culture history of the entity, not a process parameter.
Basic growth state of the edited population prior to assay transfer, such as adherent, suspension, or mixed. This describes the entity's current state rather than the assay method.

Qualitative assessment of whether the edited population has known or suspected off-target effects that may affect downstream interpretation. Record at the entity level as a property of the resulting biological material.

knockout_validation_capture.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included only measurement-session and instrument-configuration fields for the knockout validation assay: the platform identity, hardware configuration, acquisition settings, and operator-controlled validation parameters. I excluded properties of the edited cells themselves because those belong to the Entity node, and I excluded the raw readout/file details because those belong to the downstream Signal node. No already_generated fields were provided here, so I kept the schema focused on the instrument and session used to verify the perturbation, not on the validation output itself.

md_schema.descr: Name of the assay platform used to verify the CRISPR knockout, recorded at the capture stage, e.g. qPCR instrument, targeted sequencing platform, or automated genotyping system.
Manufacturer of the validation instrument used in this capture session, such as Illumina, Thermo Fisher, Bio-Rad, or equivalent vendor. Record the hardware provider for the assay platform.
Instrument model used for knockout validation capture, e.g. a specific qPCR cycler or sequencing system model. Record the exact hardware model configured for the session.
Serial number of the instrument used in the validation capture session, recorded as the hardware identifier for traceability. Use the manufacturer's serial number string.

Type of validation assay run on the edited cells, such as qPCR-based confirmation, targeted amplicon sequencing, or reporter-based genotyping. This describes the configured capture assay, not the biological sample.
Total reaction volume used in the validation assay, reported in µL at the time of instrument setup. Include the actual capture-session volume used for verification measurements.
Number of acquisition cycles or PCR cycles used during the validation capture session, measured as the instrument setting that governs readout collection. Record the actual cycle count used.

Annealing temperature in degrees Celsius used for validation amplification, recorded as part of the capture configuration when qPCR or related amplification-based validation is performed. Typical values are assay-specific and should reflect the measured instrument setting.

Instrument or assay threshold used to call knockout validation success, such as fluorescence threshold, cycle cutoff, or readout cutoff. Record the configured decision threshold applied during capture.

Quality status of the validation capture session, indicating whether the instrument run and assay setup produced acceptable measurements for downstream interpretation. Use a simple categorical QC flag.

knockout_validation_signal.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only raw data artefact fields: file format, size, dimensionality, storage location, and technical quality metrics for the knockout validation readout. I excluded assay configuration and instrument settings because those belong to the Capture node, and I excluded interpretation such as whether the knockout succeeded because that would be derivative or analysis-level information rather than the raw signal. No already_generated fields were provided here, so I kept the schema specific to the validation readout artifact itself.

md_schema.descr: Name of the raw validation readout file produced by the knockout assay, recorded exactly as stored on disk or in the data system. Use a representative example such as 'sample123_validation.csv' or 'run45.qpcr'.
Digital file format of the raw knockout validation readout, such as CSV, TXT, XLSX, FASTQ, or proprietary instrument export. Record the format of the signal artifact itself.
Size of the raw validation file in bytes at the time of ingestion or storage. This is a technical property of the signal artifact and should reflect the actual file size.
Number of rows in the raw validation signal matrix or table, representing the measurement dimensionality of the artifact. Record the row count as stored in the file.
Number of columns in the raw validation signal matrix or table, representing the measurement dimensionality of the artifact. Record the column count as stored in the file.
Primary storage path, URI, or object-store location of the raw validation readout. Use a concrete location string such as a filesystem path or bucket URI.
Checksum for the raw validation file used to verify integrity during transfer or storage, recorded as the MD5 digest string.

Technical quality flag for the raw validation readout, indicating whether the artifact is complete and readable for downstream processing. This is a signal-level QC property, not a biological interpretation.

cell_lysis_and_protein_extraction.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included fields for how the lysis and protein extraction were performed: lysis buffer composition, mechanical/chemical disruption method, extraction temperatures and times, protease inhibitor use, and process-level yield/QC. I excluded edited-cell properties because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded protein extract sample properties because those belong to the downstream Entity node. I also avoided any mass spectrometry configuration or raw file details because those belong further downstream to Capture and Signal nodes.

md_schema.descr: Composition of the lysis buffer used to disrupt the edited cells for proteomics sample preparation, including key detergents, salts, and additives. Record the formulation used at the process stage.
Method used to lyse the edited cells, such as chemical lysis, sonication, bead beating, or freeze-thaw. Record the primary disruption approach used during protein extraction.

Temperature in degrees Celsius used during lysis and protein extraction, recorded for the processing step when cells were disrupted and proteins were solubilized. Typical proteomics-compatible values are low-temperature conditions such as 4 C or ice-cold processing.
Duration in minutes for the lysis and protein extraction step, measured from the start of disruption through completion of soluble protein recovery.
Whether protease inhibitors were added during lysis and extraction to preserve protein integrity. Record as a process-level yes/no field.

Total soluble protein yield recovered from the edited cells after lysis, reported in milligrams at the end of the extraction process. Typical values are assay-dependent and should reflect the actual yield obtained.
Cleanup or clarification method applied after lysis, such as centrifugation, filtration, precipitation, or desalting, used to make the extract proteomics-compatible.
Overall quality assessment of the lysis and protein extraction step, indicating whether the preparation yielded a proteomics-compatible extract suitable for downstream mass spectrometry.

protein_extract_sample.reasoning: This is an Entity node representing the prepared protein extract itself, so I included intrinsic sample properties: extract identity, concentration, volume, purity, storage, and aliquoting status. I excluded the lysis and cleanup protocol details because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I excluded mass spectrometry configuration because that belongs to the downstream Capture node. No already_generated fields were provided here, so I avoided overlap by keeping the schema strictly about what the protein extract IS at the time it becomes the input sample for MS.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the prepared protein extract sample produced from the edited cancer cells, e.g. an internal sample code or barcode. Record the sample identity at the entity stage before mass spectrometry.

Protein concentration of the prepared extract, reported in mg/mL at the time of sample handoff to mass spectrometry. Typical values are assay-specific and should reflect the measured concentration of the entity sample.
Total volume of the prepared protein extract available for downstream mass spectrometry, reported in µL at the time of transfer or aliquoting.
Estimated purity or cleanliness of the protein extract, expressed as a percent of protein-rich material relative to contaminants. Record the sample-level estimate before MS analysis.

Temperature in degrees Celsius at which the protein extract sample is stored before downstream mass spectrometry, such as -80 C or 4 C. Record the storage condition as an intrinsic sample property at the time of handoff/storage.
Whether the protein extract was split into aliquots before mass spectrometry, recorded as a property of the sample form factor. Use true if aliquoted and false if kept as a single bulk sample.

Qualitative assessment of the extract's stability prior to analysis, such as whether the sample is intact, degraded, or partially degraded. This describes the sample state rather than the process used to make it.

mass_spectrometry_capture.reasoning: I corrected the schema by removing the colliding field capture_qc_status, since that identifier was already generated for an earlier Capture step in this DAG and must not be repeated. I kept the rest of the fields within Capture territory for the mass spectrometry acquisition session: hardware identity, acquisition configuration, and run-level operating parameters. I did not add signal- or derivative-level fields, and I continued to exclude protein extract sample properties because those belong upstream to the Entity node.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the mass spectrometer used for proteomics capture, recorded as the hardware provider for the acquisition session, e.g. Thermo Fisher, Bruker, Sciex, or Agilent.
Instrument model used for the mass spectrometry capture session, e.g. Orbitrap Fusion, Q Exactive, timsTOF, or equivalent. Record the exact configured hardware model.
Serial number of the mass spectrometer used in this capture session, recorded for traceability of the hardware configuration.
Ionization mode configured for the mass spectrometry acquisition, describing how analytes were introduced into the mass spectrometer. Typical proteomics values include electrospray ionization.
Type of mass analyzer used during acquisition, such as Orbitrap, time-of-flight, ion trap, or quadrupole configuration. Record the analyzer setting actually used in the capture session.
MS acquisition mode used for the capture session, such as data-dependent acquisition or data-independent acquisition. Record the configured mode that governs how spectra were collected.
Mass-to-charge scan range in m/z used during acquisition, recorded as the instrument setting for the capture session. Provide the approximate lower and upper bound used for the run.
Total runtime of the mass spectrometry acquisition in minutes, measured from run start to run end for the capture session.
Chromatographic column temperature in degrees Celsius during MS capture when liquid chromatography is coupled to the instrument. Record the actively controlled acquisition temperature.

raw_ms_spectra.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only raw data artefact fields for the unprocessed MS spectra: file naming, format, size, dimensionality, storage location, and technical quality metrics. I excluded capture settings because those belong to the upstream Capture node, and I excluded spectral interpretation or protein identification because those belong to downstream Process/Derivative nodes. I also avoided the previously generated field name capture_qc_status due to DAG-wide field collision, replacing it with a signal-specific quality field that describes the raw spectra artifact instead of the acquisition session.

md_schema.descr: Name of the raw mass spectra file as stored after acquisition, recorded exactly as the file name or run export identifier, e.g. 'run001.raw' or 'sampleA.mzML'.
Digital file format of the raw mass spectra artifact, such as RAW, mzML, mzXML, or vendor-specific export format. Record the format of the unprocessed signal file.
Size of the raw spectra file in bytes at the time of ingestion or storage, reflecting the technical footprint of the signal artifact.
Total number of spectra contained in the raw MS file, measured as a technical dimensionality property of the signal artifact. Report the count as stored in the raw file.
Number of MS scans recorded in the raw spectra file, representing the acquisition dimensionality of the signal artifact. Record the total scan count for the file.
Filesystem path, database location, or object-store URI where the raw mass spectra file is stored, e.g. an S3 URI or local directory path.
SHA-256 checksum string for the raw spectra file, used to verify integrity after transfer or storage.

Technical quality flag for the raw mass spectra artifact, indicating whether the file is complete and readable for downstream processing. This describes the signal itself rather than the acquisition session.

spectral_processing.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only computation/pipeline fields for turning raw spectra into proteomic features: software identity, version, repository, key algorithmic settings, database parameters, and process-level QC. I excluded raw spectra file properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded identified protein result fields because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, but I also avoided reusing acquisition-specific QC names from earlier capture steps by using process-specific quality fields instead.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or analysis pipeline used to process raw MS spectra into proteomic features, recorded as the process agent identity, e.g. MaxQuant, Proteome Discoverer, MSFragger, or an in-house pipeline.
Version of the processing software used for spectral analysis, recorded at the time the pipeline was executed. Use the exact release string, e.g. '2.4.0' or '1.6.15.0'.
Software repository or source location for the spectral processing pipeline, such as a GitHub URL, container registry, or vendor download page. Record where the processing implementation came from.
Proteolytic enzyme specificity assumed during database search and peptide assignment, such as trypsin or Lys-C. Record the processing setting used to interpret spectra.
Maximum number of missed cleavages permitted in the spectral search and peptide identification step, recorded as an integer algorithm parameter.
Precursor mass tolerance used during spectral matching, reported in parts per million (ppm) as an algorithm parameter for the processing step.
Fragment ion mass tolerance used during spectral matching, reported in daltons (Da) as an algorithm parameter for the processing step.
Reference protein database used for peptide/protein identification, such as UniProt human proteome or a custom FASTA. Record the database identity used in the processing pipeline.
Target-decoy or related strategy used to estimate false discovery rates during spectral processing, such as reverse, shuffled, or concatenated decoy generation.

Quality status of the spectral processing run, indicating whether the pipeline completed successfully and produced usable proteomic features for downstream interpretation. Use a process-level QC flag.

identified_proteins.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed-result fields describing the protein identifications themselves: the inferred protein identity, quantification values, confidence/statistical support, replicate context, and result-level QC. I excluded raw spectra properties because those belong to the upstream Signal node, and I excluded spectral processing settings because those belong to the upstream Process node. I also avoided any fields already generated for other nodes and kept this schema focused on the computed proteomic output rather than the experimental inputs or instrument configuration.

md_schema.descr: Identifier of the inferred protein-level feature produced by processing the spectra, typically a UniProt accession or other protein database identifier. Record the computed protein identity at the derivative stage.
Common or database protein name corresponding to the identified protein feature, recorded as the computed result of spectral inference.
Gene symbol associated with the identified protein, if available from the reference database, e.g. TP53 or EGFR. Record the mapped symbol for the computed protein feature.
Number of unique or razor peptides supporting the protein identification, recorded as a count from the computational result for the given knockout condition and replicate.
Quantified abundance of the identified protein derived from the processed spectra, reported in the analysis' native abundance units or normalized intensity scale used by the pipeline.
Unit or scale used for the protein abundance value, such as LFQ intensity, iBAQ, spectral counts, or normalized relative abundance. Record the quantification scale used for this derivative result.
Estimated false discovery rate for the protein identification, reported as a percent confidence metric produced by the computational pipeline for this result.
Biological or technical replicate number associated with the identified protein result, recorded as an integer so downstream users can link the derivative output to the screening replicate.

Label for the knockout condition under which the protein was identified, such as the targeted gene or perturbation batch identifier. This is a derivative context field tying the computed protein result to the edit condition.
Quality flag for the computed protein identification result, indicating whether the identification passed result-level thresholds for downstream causal analysis. Use a derivative-level QC flag.

literature_support.reasoning: This is a Signal node that represents external reference artifacts, so I included only bibliographic and technical document properties: citation identity, source, persistent identifiers, access location, and basic support status. I excluded capture settings and biological interpretation because those belong to other nodes, and I avoided duplicating protein-identification or causal-claim fields already covered by downstream analytical nodes. Since this node is marked external, I focused on how the reference is stored and cited rather than on experimental provenance.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the curated literature reference entry, such as an internal citation key or database record ID. Record the reference artifact identity at the signal stage.

Full bibliographic citation string for the supporting literature reference, e.g. authors, title, journal, year, and volume/pages. Store the exact citation used to support the interaction or causal claim.
Digital Object Identifier for the literature reference, recorded as a persistent identifier string when available, e.g. '10.1038/s41586-020-...' .
PubMed identifier for the literature reference, recorded as a string or numeric-like string when available. Use the PMID associated with the supporting publication.
Database, bibliography manager, or curation source from which the literature reference was obtained, such as PubMed, CrossRef, Google Scholar, or an internal curation database.
Resolvable URL or landing-page link for the supporting literature reference, recorded as the access location of the citation artifact.

Type of evidence the reference provides for the protein interaction or causal claim, such as direct experiment, review, or computational support. Record how the cited literature supports the screening result.
Short text summary of the specific claim supported by the reference, such as a reported interaction, pathway relationship, or causal inference relevant to the screened proteins.
Date on which the reference was retrieved or curated into the dataset, recorded as a date value for provenance of the external literature artifact.
Quality flag for the curated reference artifact, indicating whether the citation is complete and usable for downstream metadata assembly. Use a signal-level QC flag for the reference record.

metadata_table_generation.reasoning: This is a Process node that performs integration of upstream validated readouts, protein identifications, and literature references into a structured table. So I included only process/pipeline fields that describe how the table was assembled: software, version, integration rules, join keys, filtering criteria, and process-level QC. I excluded the actual table content because that belongs to the downstream Derivative node, and I avoided repeating upstream signal/derivative identifiers or capture settings. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, but I kept the schema focused on the assembly workflow rather than the final metadata table contents.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software, script, or pipeline used to assemble the screening metadata table from validated readouts, identified proteins, and literature references. Record the process agent identity, e.g. Python, R, or an in-house ETL pipeline.

Version of the table assembly software or pipeline used to generate the final metadata table, recorded at the time the integration was run. Use the exact release or interpreter version string, e.g. '3.11' for Python.

Method used to combine upstream inputs into the final metadata table, such as rule-based merge, relational join, manual curation, or hybrid integration. Record the assembly strategy used in the process.

Primary key or matching field used to align validation readouts, protein identifications, and literature records during table assembly, e.g. knockout target gene, sample barcode, or replicate identifier. Record the field name used for joining inputs.

Rule or algorithm used to assign the causal relationship type in the metadata table, such as curated ontology mapping, heuristic scoring, or manual annotation. Record the process used to derive the causal summary field.

Criteria used to decide which literature references were included in the final table, such as direct evidence only, PMID availability, or relevance to the knockout target. Record the curation rule applied during table assembly.

Threshold used to exclude low-confidence entries during metadata table assembly, reported in the native scale of the pipeline, such as minimum FDR or minimum validation score. Record the filtering criterion applied to upstream rows.
Version identifier for the output metadata table schema produced by this assembly process, e.g. 'v1.0'. Record the structural version of the integrated table, not the data content.
Overall quality assessment of the metadata table assembly process, indicating whether the integration completed successfully and produced a consistent structured table. Use a process-level QC flag.

metadata_table.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only fields that describe the computed final table itself: table identity, dimensions, column/schema characteristics, content completeness, and result-level quality. I excluded the assembly software and merging rules because those belong to the upstream Process node, and I avoided repeating upstream protein, validation, and literature identifiers because those are already represented in their own nodes. I also kept the schema focused on the final reusable artifact rather than the experimental inputs used to create it.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the final structured metadata table produced by the workflow, e.g. an internal dataset table ID or versioned record name. Record the derivative artifact identity for the integrated screening table.
Storage or serialization format of the final metadata table, such as CSV, TSV, XLSX, Parquet, or database table. Record the computed artifact's file or table format.
Total number of rows in the final metadata table, reported as the size of the computed derivative artifact. Record the count as stored in the output table.
Total number of columns in the final metadata table, reported as the schema width of the computed derivative artifact.

Comma-separated list or equivalent representation of the final table column names, capturing the structure of the integrated screening metadata output. Provide the names as stored in the derivative artifact.
Percent of expected table fields populated across rows in the final metadata table, used as a result-level completeness metric for the derivative artifact.

Summary of the distribution of causal relationship types represented in the final table, such as counts or proportions of activation, inhibition, or association labels. Record the computed result summary for the integrated output.
Version label of the final metadata table artifact, e.g. 'v1.0', as produced by the integration workflow. Record the derivative version identifier.
Overall quality flag for the final structured metadata table, indicating whether the output is suitable for dataset release or downstream reuse. Use a derivative-level QC status.
